title: Release lore 0.8.0: version bump, CHANGELOG, README version lines, tag
description:
Cut 0.8.0 from dev. Dispatched by opum-agent under OPAG-248 (operator goal: resolve open lore-cli and quest-cli issues and release the updated pair). The six pre-release defects are landed: LCLI-534, 535, 536, 512, 533, 522.

WHY 0.8.0 AND NOT 0.7.1, ratified by opum-agent: dev carries a NEW COMMAND (lore types, LCLI-537), a NEW CONFIG KEY (profile.strict_types, LCLI-538) and a NEW FAILURE MODE in a shipped gate (committed-schema drift detection in lore check, LCLI-539). Minor-bump shaped under 0.x.

THE PAIR IS NON-LOCKSTEP BY DECISION, not by drift. quest-cli ships 0.9.0 (their v0.8.0 tag is already pushed with dev past it, and they will not re-point a pushed tag). OPAG-142 already established lore 0.7.0 + quest 0.7.1 as a QUALIFIED non-lockstep pair, so 'release the pair' means released TOGETHER, not numbered alike. Do not pin a version comparison anywhere to decide compatibility -- detect by presence.

PUBLICATION IS NOT PART OF THIS TASK. LCLI-482 is open and unresolved: OIDC trusted publishing cannot authenticate for this repository (GitHub issues immutable-format subject claims for repos recreated after 2026-07-15; lore-cli was recreated 2026-09-10; npm Trusted Publishing matches the classic form and returns E404). The only working path is scripts/publish-release.sh, which requires a human at a TTY for npm's browser OTP. Publication is also tier 3 and goes to this session's own user directly, never on an orchestrator's say-so.

COUPLINGS TO HONOUR AT TAG TIME:
- opum-marketplace federates skills/ BY TAG. Send them the tag name, tag object SHA, the commit it peels to, and the resolved skills/ tree SHA, then a second message when npm actually publishes (LCLI-469). Their check does not go red when we tag -- it re-resolves an immutable pinned ref -- so this is bookkeeping, not an incident.
- opum-cli-e2e needs the six per-platform ladybug-package-qualification-<platform> artifacts for its --lore-report rows. These come from a release.yml workflow_dispatch with publish:false (a build, no registry action), NOT from the tag: release.yml has no tag trigger.
- The new lore check drift gate is a fleet compatibility event. Sibling repos pin lore by hand in their own workflows, so it reaches them only when they bump that line; the heads-up goes out with the pin move.
implementationNotes:
HANDOFF 2026-09-19T00:5xZ, session recycled mid-release. READ THE REGISTRY BEFORE TRUSTING ANY STATE SENTENCE IN THIS NOTE, INCLUDING MINE -- the publish was in flight when this was written and npm's read API lags its own writes by minutes on this package set. First command: npm view @opum-ai/lore@0.8.0 version; npm view @opum-ai/lore dist-tags.latest.

STATE AT WRITING, each line naming the command that produced it.
 - All SIX platform packages are PUBLISHED AND READABLE at 0.8.0 with dist-tags.latest=0.8.0 (npm view @opum-ai/lore-<platform>@0.8.0 version, all six returned 0.8.0).
 - The ROOT @opum-ai/lore@0.8.0 was ACCEPTED BY NPM. scripts/publish-release.sh printed '+ @opum-ai/lore@0.8.0' and then '+latest: @opum-ai/lore@0.8.0' for the dist-tag move, both npm's own success lines, followed by npm's notice 'Your package is being processed and may take a few minutes to become available.'
 - At the same moment the READ API still said ABSENT: npm view -> E404, and GET registry.npmjs.org/@opum-ai%2Flore/0.8.0 -> HTTP 404, with dist-tags.latest reading 0.7.0. THE WRITE SUCCEEDED AND THE READ HAD NOT CAUGHT UP. Those are not in conflict; it is the same lag measured twice already tonight.
 - The script was left running its own post-publish visibility poll (read-only, 1800s window). Harmless if it timed out; its timeout is not evidence of failure.

DO NOT REDO ANY OF THIS -- each item cost real time to establish.
 1. DO NOT RE-RUN THE PUBLISH to 'fix' an absent root. npm forbids republishing a version. A re-attempt over a version npm is still processing is what produced tonight's whole incident: it returns E409 'Cannot publish over previously staged version', which reads like a 2FA hold and is NOT one.
 2. DO NOT touch the npmjs.com UI to approve or reject anything. There is nothing to approve. I sent the operator looking for a reject button that does not exist; the UI showed the version as VALIDATING, which is npm processing an upload, not a stage awaiting a human.
 3. DO NOT 'fix' or bypass LCLI-502's visibility gate. It performed exactly as designed all night: it refused to publish the root while linux-x64 was unreadable, which is the single reason no consumer could ever resolve a half-published 0.8.0. Two independent implementations (mine and quest-cli's) held the same line tonight. If you find the root unpublished and a platform package missing, THAT IS THE GATE WORKING.
 4. DO NOT ask anyone to publish a missing platform package. Publishing is operator-only and it has already been done.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY OUTSTANDING:
 a. Confirm the root and dist-tags.latest are readable at 0.8.0. If they are, the release is COMPLETE -- nothing further to publish.
 b. Then tell opum-cli-e2e (waiting): its 'installed lore launcher is byte-identical to the published root package' row is the last of five and resolves the moment the root is readable. Its pre-publish run stands at 414/418 with 6/6 platform digests corroborated against our qualification reports.
 c. Then tell opum-marketplace (waiting): the SECOND of the two messages LCLI-469 owes them, the one sent when dist-tags.latest actually moves. Their pin stays at v0.7.0 until then, by their own design. Their skills/ baseline needs NO change: skills/ at v0.8.0 is byte-identical to v0.7.0 (tree 2998f74d077845f8ad73f83aa296e37e034378a4, and git log v0.7.0..v0.8.0 -- skills/ is empty).
 d. Close LCLI-543 once (a) holds.

RELEASE FACTS, so nothing is re-derived: tag v0.8.0 is an ANNOTATED tag, object cfd84892a21d4ccebdeb347dc533bc208a82e818, peeling to commit 4d4a1bfba1a1e46d362f0ab2370e250e47c8253c -- the two SHAs differ and the peel is the commit. main and dev are both at that commit; both post-push promotion assertions passed (trees equal at 86c8c175, main is an ancestor of dev, zero merge commits). Build-and-qualify run 35409381009 (workflow_dispatch, publish:false) produced the six ladybug-package-qualification-<platform> artifacts.

LESSON WORTH KEEPING, and the reason this note is long: a REGISTRY READ CANNOT SEPARATE published / slow / validating / staged. Only a write can, and even a write's error text is ambiguous -- E409 says the word 'staged' for the validation holding area too. The npmjs.com UI is the only surface that names which one it is. I reached the wrong conclusion twice from reads tonight and was corrected both times by someone looking at a different surface.

ALSO AMENDED THIS SESSION: LCLI-482 now carries a note recording that its 'human at a TTY for a browser OTP' claim is STALE -- publish-release.sh reads a granular npm token from the macOS Keychain and there is no OTP. What remains true there is only that OIDC is broken, so release.yml cannot publish and 0.8.0 carries no provenance attestation. That record was misinforming every session that read it (operator report, opum-agent's OPAG-265).

Session write at 2026-09-19T01:02:20Z. Branch dev, 2 uncommitted file(s). Written by the opum-workflow write hook (0.8.6+269bf00c7e84 (/Users/jdnewhouse/.claude/plugins/cache/opum-fleet/opum-workflow/0.8.6)), not by the model.

ADDENDUM, after the handoff note above was written.

THE RELEASE IS COMPLETE. Verified by read, not by write receipt: npm view @opum-ai/lore@0.8.0 -> 0.8.0, and npm view @opum-ai/lore dist-tags --json -> latest 0.8.0. All six platform packages were already readable at 0.8.0 with their own latest tags moved. So item (a) of the outstanding list above is DONE and the successor does not need to confirm it again -- though re-reading costs one command and the note's opening instruction still stands.

STILL OUTSTANDING for the successor: tell opum-cli-e2e the root is readable (its fifth row resolves on its own), send opum-marketplace the second LCLI-469 message now that dist-tags.latest has actually moved, and close LCLI-543.

ONE NEW DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS SAME BRANCH, filed as LCLI-544. bun.lock still pinned @opum-ai/lore-*@0.7.0 after the 0.8.0 bump, so bun install --frozen-lockfile began failing across EVERY CI job at the setup-bun step -- on dev and on every open PR. Regenerated and verified: frozen install exits 0.

The mechanism matters more than the fix and is why LCLI-544 exists. At bump time the 0.8.0 packages did not exist on npm, so bun could not resolve them and left the lockfile alone; --frozen-lockfile compared two things that still agreed and PASSED. Publishing made them resolvable and the same unchanged lockfile went stale instantly. PR #180 and #181 were genuinely green and the next PR genuinely red with NO source change between them. The defect was latent from the bump and armed by the publish.

So: a green bump PR is not evidence its lockfile is current, when the bump names versions that are not published yet. The check that would catch it needs the registry, and a registry check necessarily fails before the publish for a version that is supposed not to exist. LCLI-544 records the two candidate fixes.
finalSummary:
lore 0.8.0 IS RELEASED, PUBLISHED AND QUALIFIED. Closing on a READ, not on the publisher's exit code: npm view @opum-ai/lore@0.8.0 -> 0.8.0 and dist-tags.latest -> 0.8.0, with all six @opum-ai/lore-<platform> packages likewise live at 0.8.0 with their own latest moved. This note supersedes the handoff note above, which was written while the publish was still in flight and correctly told its reader to re-read the registry before trusting it.

QUALIFIED AS A PAIR by opum-cli-e2e against quest 0.9.0: 460 rows, 459 pass, 0 FAIL, 1 BLOCKED (the routine out-of-band scale job, deliberately unbound). Gated against the previous baseline v0.7.1-lore0.7.0-pair: exit 0, NO REGRESSION, 0 FIXED, 0 REGRESSED, 0 OTHER; 14 ADDED / 4 REMOVED with the removals pairing exactly to additions as version-identity renames. baselines/v0.9.0-lore0.8.0-pair is cut (opum-cli-e2e#207). All three lore-side rows green, including the published-tarball-vs-qualified-digest corroboration at 6/6 and the launcher byte-identity row.

THE PAIR IS DELIBERATELY NON-LOCKSTEP: lore 0.8.0 + quest 0.9.0. quest is at 0.9.0 because it BURNED 0.8.0 -- tagged it, moved 15 commits past, and correctly refused to re-point a pushed tag -- so 0.9.0 is an artifact of quest's release mechanics, not a larger change set. Ruled by opum-agent after the operator challenged the numbering. 'The pair' means released and qualified TOGETHER, not numbered alike; compatibility is detected by presence, never by comparing versions.

WHAT SHIPPED: lore types (LCLI-537), profile.strict_types (LCLI-538), committed-schema drift detection in lore check (LCLI-539), and six defect fixes -- LCLI-534 (multi-word type unreachable from its own slug), LCLI-535 (lore new did not scaffold declared sections), LCLI-536 (--template double-appended .md), LCLI-512 (lore export --help advertised a version its parser rejects), LCLI-533 (docker/e2e/selftest.sh failed green), LCLI-522 (lore link clobbered concurrent tracker edits). Plus LCLI-540's relation qualifiers in retained snapshots, staying at lore-retained-snapshot/1 so older snapshots still validate.

RELEASE ARTIFACTS: annotated tag v0.8.0, object cfd84892a21d4ccebdeb347dc533bc208a82e818, peeling to commit 4d4a1bfba1a1e46d362f0ab2370e250e47c8253c (the two differ; the peel is the commit). main and dev both at that commit, both promotion assertions passed. Build-and-qualify run 35409381009 (workflow_dispatch, publish:false) produced the six per-platform qualification artifacts handed to opum-cli-e2e. No provenance attestation, as with 0.7.0/0.6.2/0.6.1 -- OIDC remains broken (LCLI-482) so the release went out through the manual script, which cannot mint one. Expected, not tampering.

TWO DEFECTS THIS RELEASE ITSELF PRODUCED, both recorded rather than smoothed over. LCLI-544: bun.lock still pinned 0.7.0 after the bump, taking out CI on dev and every open PR at the setup-bun step -- latent from the bump and ARMED BY THE PUBLISH, because --frozen-lockfile passed at bump time by comparing two things that still agreed while the 0.8.0 packages did not yet exist. Fixed and landed; the gate gap is LCLI-544. And the npm publish of linux-x64 required a retry after an E409 whose 'previously staged' wording I misread as a 2FA hold -- it was npm's validation holding area, visible as VALIDATING in the web UI and nowhere else. A registry READ cannot separate published / slow / validating / staged; only a write can, and even its error text is ambiguous.

COUPLINGS DISCHARGED: opum-marketplace received both LCLI-469 messages (tag-cut and dist-tags-moved) and its skills/ baseline needs no change -- skills/ at v0.8.0 is byte-identical to v0.7.0, tree 2998f74d077845f8ad73f83aa296e37e034378a4, with git log v0.7.0..v0.8.0 -- skills/ empty. opum-cli-e2e received the six qualification artifacts and has cut the baseline.

STILL OPEN AND NOT PART OF THIS TASK: LCLI-544 (the lockfile gate), and two of the three OPAG-265 remedies -- putting the live publish fact where a session looks at publish time, and making publish-release.sh fail loudly when the keychain entry is missing instead of degrading silently into the OTP path. The third, amending LCLI-482's stale record, is done.
